study_type_evidence.quote: In vivo experiments were performed with 6-week-old male C57BL/6J mice (stock no. 000664) purchased from Jackson Laboratories.
Activity of native exendin and conjugates was assessed in vitro by quantifying intracellular cAMP release
One patient plasma sample previously tested negative for PEG antibody and two that were tested positive were diluted 1:400

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: 6-week-old male C57BL/6J, maintained on 60 kCal% fat diet; EG3 fed-glucose cohort used at 8 weeks
in_vivo_species.quote: In vivo experiments were performed with 6-week-old male C57BL/6J mice (stock no. 000664) purchased from Jackson Laboratories.

ex_vivo_detail: Anti-PEG direct and competitive ELISAs used plasma samples drawn from patients (one anti-PEG negative, two anti-PEG positive from a Phase II Krystexxa trial); the plasma was removed from the body and then treated (diluted, incubated with coated antigen). No animal tissue/serum incubation assay was reported.
in_vitro_detail: Intracellular cAMP ELISA in baby hamster kidney (BHK) cells stably transfected with rat GLP-1R, to derive EC50 of exendin and conjugates.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Blood samples were collected via tail vein at various time points for fluorescence quantification. Data were analyzed using a non-compartmental fit (solid lines)
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma concentration versus time after a single s.c. dose of Alexa Fluor 488-labeled exendin (panel c) and of the 54.6 kDa EG9, 55.6 kDa EG3 and 71.6 kDa EG3 conjugates (panel d); sampling 40 s to 120 h.

bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence quantification of Alexa Fluor 488-labeled constructs in plasma (excitation 485 nm, emission 535 nm, Victor multilabel plate reader); non-compartmental analysis with PK Solutions 2.0
bioanalytical_quote: Blood samples were centrifuged ... to extract the plasma for fluorescence reading at excitation 485 nm and emission 535 nm on a Victor multilabel plate reader
notes: PK (Table 2) reported for four constructs only: unmodified exendin, 54.6 kDa EG9, 55.6 kDa EG3, 71.6 kDa EG3; PK dose (75 nmol/kg s.c.) differs from the efficacy dose (25 nmol/kg s.c.). Half-lives are from a non-compartmental fit of a fluorescence signal, not of intact peptide. No amino-acid sequence for exendin or any conjugate appears anywhere in the body text or figure captions, so all sequences are recorded as 'not reported'. Ex vivo classification refers solely to the use of patient-derived plasma as the anti-PEG antibody source in the direct/competitive ELISAs; no serum-stability assay was performed. Glucose (1.5 g/kg i.p. for IPGTT) is a challenge agent and is not listed as a test article.
